demographics.narrative:
New Zealand's estimated resident population was 5,372,400 at 30 September 2026, according to provisional figures, after growth of 41,100 people (0.8 percent) over the year.{{1}} Natural increase was 18,500 and net migration added 22,600.{{1}} The median age was 39.4 years for females and 37.8 years for males.{{1}} At the 2023 Census, 67.8 percent of people identified as European, 17.8 percent as Māori, 17.3 percent as Asian and 8.9 percent as Pacific peoples, with some people identifying with more than one ethnicity.{{2}} About 84 percent of people live in urban areas, on the World Bank's definition.{{3}}

The population is aging. About 900,000 people were aged 65 and over at 30 June 2025, roughly 17 percent of residents.{{4}} Registered births numbered 57,705 in 2025, and the total fertility rate fell to 1.55 births per woman, the lowest December-year rate on record.{{5}} Period life expectancy at birth for 2023 to 2025 was 80.4 years for males and 83.7 years for females, up 0.3 years for males and 0.2 years for females on 2022 to 2024.{{5}} Māori and Pacific peoples have shorter life expectancy than New Zealanders of European ethnicity.{{6}} This points to rising demand for chronic and age-related care in a small, high-income market served mainly by a tax-funded public system.

government.narrative:
New Zealand is a constitutional monarchy, and Governor-General Dame Cindy Kiro, whose term runs to 31 March 2027, represents the King and appoints the government after an election.{{1}}{{2}} The 7 November 2026 general election has not yet produced one. Provisional results give National, ACT and New Zealand First 67 seats, a narrow majority ahead of the Labour, Green and Te Pāti Māori bloc, with seven for the new Opportunity Party.{{3}} Special votes, about a seventh of the total and usually favoring the left, will be added in a final count on 27 November and could remove that majority.{{4}} Until then Prime Minister Christopher Luxon leads a caretaker government, with the previous ministers staying in office, and formal coalition negotiations are not expected before the final count.{{5}}{{6}}

Health is run centrally. Simeon Brown is Minister of Health, and ministers keep their posts under the caretaker convention.{{7}}{{5}} The Ministry of Health (Manatū Hauora) oversees the system, and Health New Zealand (Te Whatu Ora) has delivered public services nationally since 2022{{9}} through four regions (Northern, Midland, Central and South Island) that are divided into districts.{{8}} The 2030 targets are 90 percent of cancer patients treated within 31 days of the decision to treat, 95 percent of children immunized at 24 months, 95 percent of emergency department patients admitted, discharged or transferred within six hours, and 95 percent waiting under four months for specialist assessment and for elective treatment.{{10}} A sixth target, 80 percent of people seeing a general practice provider within a week, is measured from 1 July 2026.{{11}}

economy.narrative:
New Zealand is a high-income economy, with GDP of about 305 billion international dollars at purchasing power parity in 2025, or about 57,350 per person.{{1}}{{2}} GDP rose 0.2 percent in the June 2026 quarter, after a 0.9 percent rise in the March quarter, and grew 1.7 percent over the year ended June 2026.{{3}} Unemployment reached 5.7 percent in the September 2026 quarter, with 174,000 people out of work, the highest rate since the September 2015 quarter.{{5}}

The Treasury's Pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update, presented on 29 September 2026, describes an economic recovery that has been delayed, first by the hit to confidence from United States tariffs in 2025 and then by the conflict in the Middle East.{{4}} Stronger tax revenue in 2025/26 left the deficit, measured as OBEGALx, $3.3 billion (US$1.87 billion) smaller than projected in Budget 2026, and the Treasury expects both OBEGALx and OBEGAL to reach surplus in 2028/29.{{4}} It warns that by 2030/31 New Zealand Superannuation and finance costs will take about 28 percent of the tax take, and that over the long term, unless checked, demographics will make the fiscal position unsustainable.{{4}} Projected financial improvements at Health New Zealand also help the fiscal outlook.{{4}}

disease_prevalence.narrative:
The Ministry of Health's Health and Independence Report 2025 records 38,207 deaths in 2023 on preliminary data, an age-standardized rate of 375.6 per 100,000.{{7}} Cancer was the leading cause (108.8 deaths per 100,000), followed by ischemic heart disease (41.9) and cerebrovascular disease (18.7).{{7}} That year there were 10,676 cancer deaths and 29,719 new cancer registrations.{{7}} Stats NZ counted 37,491 deaths registered in 2025.{{2}} An estimated 365,867 people had diabetes in 2025, an age-standardized prevalence of 48.6 per 1,000, up from 34.3 in 2011 and highest among Pacific peoples (139.8 per 1,000).{{4}}

Risk factors are widespread. In the 2024/25 New Zealand Health Survey, 34.2 percent of adults were obese, up from 31.3 percent in 2019/20, and 46.2 percent met physical activity guidelines.{{5}} The 2025/26 survey, published on 18 November 2026, put daily smoking at 5.9 percent of adults, the first reading below 6 percent, though 13.9 percent of Māori adults still smoked daily, and daily vaping at 11.2 percent.{{6}} In 2024/25, 16.6 percent of adults drank hazardously and 14.3 percent reported high or very high psychological distress, up from 7.4 percent in 2019/20.{{5}} The burden points to sustained demand in cardiology, oncology, neurology and metabolic care.

hospitals.narrative:
OECD records show 171 hospitals in New Zealand in 2025, 92 of them public and 79 private, with 13,195 beds in all.{{1}}{{2}} Public hospitals hold about 85 percent of those beds, and at 2.48 beds per 1,000 people in 2024 the country sits well below the OECD mean of 4.25.{{2}}{{10}} Health New Zealand runs the public hospitals, and private hospitals concentrate on elective surgery. Southern Cross Healthcare has ten wholly owned hospitals and seven joint venture partnerships, Evolution Healthcare describes six hospitals plus day hospitals and a maternity hospital, and Allevia operates in Auckland.{{3}}{{4}}{{8}}

In 2024/25 Health New Zealand managed 1,341,270 emergency department attendances and 693,422 first specialist appointments, and 198,897 people had an elective procedure.{{5}} The agency ended 2024/25 with a deficit of $947 million (US$538 million) in its annual report, $153 million (US$86.9 million) better than budgeted, and the Treasury's consolidated accounts show a smaller deficit of $369 million (US$210 million) for 2025/26, down from $835 million (US$474 million) on that basis.{{5}}{{11}} OECD counts follow a statistical definition and differ from Health New Zealand's own facility counts. Clinical teaching follows the two medical schools: Auckland trains across Auckland, Waikato and Tauranga, and Otago trains in Wellington, Christchurch and Dunedin.{{6}}{{7}}

financing.narrative:
Current health expenditure was 10.0 percent of GDP in 2024 (provisional), above the OECD mean of 9.3 percent, and the OECD's 2025 estimate is 9.8 percent.{{1}} Per person, New Zealand spent US$6,067 in 2024 on a purchasing power parity basis, close to the OECD mean of US$6,100; the World Bank's figure of US$5,022 uses current US dollars and so is lower.{{2}}{{3}} Government schemes and compulsory insurance covered 79.8 percent of spending, out-of-pocket payments 12.7 percent and voluntary schemes 7.5 percent.{{1}} The share of GDP is below Australia, the United Kingdom, Canada and the United States.{{1}} Pharmac buys medicines within a fixed budget, and prescription copayments are capped at NZ$5 (US$2.84) per item.{{4}}

Budget 2026, released on 28 May 2026, provides more than $5.8 billion (US$3.29 billion) in new Vote Health operating funding over the forecast period, including a $1.37 billion (US$778 million) annual uplift for cost pressures and demand, and the government says total health spending will reach $34.2 billion (US$19.4 billion) in 2026/27.{{5}} It funds 24,000 additional planned care treatments and 24,000 additional cancer treatments in 2026/27, among other services.{{5}}

workforce.narrative:
New Zealand had 20,530 practicing doctors at 30 June 2025, up 2.6 percent on 2024, or 388.3 per 100,000 people.{{1}} International medical graduates made up 42.1 percent of doctors responding to the Medical Council's survey and 43.5 percent of those on the register, rising above 60 percent in Whanganui and South Canterbury.{{1}} Retention is the weak point: 99 percent of New Zealand graduates are retained after one year, against 40 percent of international graduates after two years.{{1}}

On the OECD's measure of practising physicians, New Zealand had 3.72 per 1,000 people in 2024, slightly below the unweighted OECD mean of 4.02; the OECD's licensed-to-practice measure gives 3.78 against a mean of 5.71.{{2}} Nurse density is above the mean at 12.4 per 1,000, pharmacist density and hospital beds are below it, CT scanners are well above the mean, MRI units level with it and PET scanners below it, on 2024 data that include a break in New Zealand's CT series.{{3}}{{4}}{{5}}{{6}} At 30 June 2026, 80,960 nurses held annual practicing certificates, 4 percent fewer than a year earlier, and 43.5 percent of them qualified overseas.{{7}}

competitive_landscape.narrative: Ten foreign partners have active ties with New Zealand institutions, confirmed from announcements dated since October 2024. Most are university research and training links, including Johns Hopkins, the University of Texas at Austin, Southampton, the National University of Singapore and Wollongong.{{2}}{{3}} Icon Group runs the one clinical service, a cancer centre in Wellington held as a joint venture with Evolution Healthcare.{{1}} In July 2026 Health New Zealand signed an agreement with UCLPartners in London on digital and AI innovation.{{4}}
competitive_landscape.closing: New Zealand mainly sends patients abroad. Health NZ's High Cost Treatment Pool funds treatment abroad for a handful of people a year, and others pay themselves.{{5}} Inbound flows are small and regional: the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade's New Zealand Medical Treatment Scheme funds referrals for Pacific patients, and a review found 53 people treated under its overseas component.{{6}}{{7}}

recent_developments.headline: Daily smoking falls below 6 percent in the 2025/26 Health Survey
recent_developments.summary: The latest New Zealand Health Survey found 5.9 percent of adults smoking daily, the first reading below 6 percent, down from 6.7 percent. Daily vaping was 11.2 percent, and 13.9 percent of Māori adults still smoked daily.{{1}}

recent_developments.headline: Winter flu season cuts planned surgery volumes
recent_developments.summary: Health NZ figures released under the Official Information Act show planned operations fell from 38,824 in May and June to 33,778 in July and August. Volumes were still about 370 higher than in the same months of 2025.{{1}}

recent_developments.headline: General election leaves government formation open
recent_developments.summary: Provisional results give National, ACT and New Zealand First 67 seats, a narrow majority, with Opportunity holding seven. Special votes will be counted in a final result on 27 November, and Prime Minister Luxon leads a caretaker government until a coalition is formed.{{1}}{{2}}

recent_developments.headline: Health New Zealand reports gains on all five health targets
recent_developments.summary: For April to June 2026, 72.6 percent of people received elective treatment within four months, up from 63.9 percent, and 66.1 percent had a first specialist assessment. Cancer treatment within 31 days reached 87.0 percent, emergency department stays under six hours 76.3 percent, and immunization at 24 months 83.7 percent.{{1}}{{2}}

recent_developments.summary: Budget 2026 provides more than $5.8 billion (US$3.29 billion) in new Vote Health operating funding over the forecast period, including a $1.37 billion (US$778 million) annual uplift, and the government says total health spending will reach $34.2 billion (US$19.4 billion) in 2026/27.{{1}} It also lowers the bowel screening eligibility age to 56.{{1}}
